summary: Abram travels into the Negev and later returns from Egypt through it. The same noun gives a compass bearing when the bronze oxen beneath the temple basin face north, west, south and east.

senses.definition: The southern tract of the land, within which particular districts and towns can be named.

evidence.note: Judah’s towns in the Negev lie toward the border of Edom.
David names the Negev of Judah, of the Jerahmeelites and of the Kenites.
Achsah asks for springs to go with the Negev land she has received.
The singer asks Yahweh to restore his people’s fortunes like watercourses in the Negev.

senses.definition: One of the four compass directions. It describes the orientation of an object, the course of a boundary or the extent of land in view.

evidence.note: Of the twelve oxen supporting the basin, three face south.
The builders set twenty frames on the south side of the dwelling.
Yahweh tells Abram to look in all four directions from where he stands.

evidence.locator: ngb V, derivatives, ngb/ngbʾ (ngb#2 N), South
ngb V, causative, Samaritan Aramaic, Marqe 1.785, of the flood waters
ngb V, reflexive stem, Syriac, AGnEx 20.5, of the surface drying

note: The Aramaic noun supplies a direct comparison for the compass sense. The Samaritan Aramaic and Syriac verbs describe drying. Achsah’s request for springs suits a connection with dry land, but how the regional name and the compass term developed remains open.
